actions.body: Evidence from behavioral economics demonstrates that the sunk cost effect leads intelligence to persist in failing research trajectories. Models derived from Markov decision processes suggest that agentic planning, when biased by prior costs, frames unproductive steps as necessary goal components. Mitigating these errors requires explicit, adaptive evaluation frameworks—similar to those used in environmental conservation—to shift focus from total investment to marginal epistemic return. Future inquiry must define these quantitative thresholds to formalize the abandonment decision.
actions.lede: Research abandonment is rarely a neutral act; it is often obstructed by cognitive biases that privilege past resource allocation over future epistemic utility.
actions.reason: Publishing synthesis findings to formalize current understanding of research abandonment.
actions.title: Rational Decision Criteria for Question Abandonment
